newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle first-half profit jumps but shares slip.
newsitem.headline: Nestle first-half profit jumps but shares slip.

text.p: Nestle SA, the world's biggest food and beverage company, said net profit rose 20 percent in the first half of 1996, but its stock price fell Friday as investors focused instead on stagnant trading results.
Net profit swelled by a fifth compared with the year-earlier period to 1.35 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion), the company said in its interim report from Vevey, on the shores of Lake Geneva.

This was roughly in line with analysts' forecasts, but dealers seized on barely changed trading profits and Nestle's forecast that profit growth would slow in the second half of the year as reasons to mark prices down.
The stock opened at 1,417 Swiss francs ($1,143), down from the previous close at 1,423 ($1,148), and slipped briefly below 1,400 ($1,130) at midday.

"I will keep my neutral rating (for Nestle) relative to the Swiss market, but in the short term prices will continue to come under pressure," said James Amoroso, an analyst for CS Investment Research in Zurich.

He pointed to first-half trading profits that rose less than 1 percent from the year-earlier period to 2.46 billion francs ($1.99 billion). Its trading margin, which measures trading profit against sales, slipped to 8.6 percent from 9.1 percent in 1995.
"People were looking for a 9.7 margin and we got 8.6, which was very disappointing," Amoroso said.
Nestle said first-half sales rose 5.6 percent to 28.44 billion francs ($22.95 billion), boosted primarily by internal sales growth. Currency fluctuations had a slight negative effect on turnover.

"For the full year 1996, Nestle expects the favourable trend in sales to continue, and consolidated sales for the year should approach 60 billion Swiss francs $48 billion)," it said. Its 1995 sales totalled 56.48 billion Swiss francs ($45.58 billion).
But it added net profits would not rise as fast in the second half because the first-half rate was based in part on comparison with a feeble start to 1995.

Nestle posted a 1995 group net profit of 2.92 billion francs ($2.36 billion), down from 3.25 billion ($2.62 billion) in 1994, when sales of cosmetics businesses produced an exceptional gain of 306 million francs ($247 million).
